title: Beginner and fundamentals
about: Start here if you are learning to program at all, not just a new language.

links.name: freeCodeCamp
links.about: a full curriculum with certificates, entirely free, no upsell.

links.name: CS50
links.about: Harvard's introduction. Still the best first course in computer science.

links.name: The Odin Project
links.about: project-driven web development, open source and thorough.

links.name: MDN Web Docs
links.about: the reference for HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Trust it over blog posts.

links.name: Exercism
links.about: small exercises in 70 languages, with human mentors if you want them.

links.name: W3Schools
links.about: quick syntax lookups when you just need the shape of something.

links.name: Codecademy
links.about: guided interactive lessons; the basics are free.

links.name: SoloLearn
links.about: bite-sized lessons that work well on a phone.

title: Programming practice
about: Reps. The point is volume and variety, not difficulty.

links.name: HackerRank
links.about: structured tracks by language and topic, with a gentle curve.

links.name: Codewars
links.about: short katas ranked by difficulty; you see other solutions after yours.

links.name: GeeksforGeeks
links.about: enormous archive of explained problems and articles.

links.name: CodingBat
links.about: tiny Java and Python drills, ideal for the first month.

links.name: Coderbyte
links.about: challenges plus interview preparation material.

links.name: Kattis
links.about: a clean judge with problems from real contests.

title: DSA and interviews
about: Where to grind problems until the patterns become automatic.

links.name: LeetCode
links.about: the interview standard. Work by pattern, not by number.

links.name: NeetCode
links.about: the same problems, ordered so each one teaches the next.

links.name: CSES Problem Set
links.about: 300 problems that cover the whole classical syllabus.

links.name: InterviewBit
links.about: a guided path with mock interviews.

links.name: AlgoExpert
links.about: curated set with video explanations. Paid.

links.name: GeeksforGeeks
links.about: the article behind almost every algorithm you will search for.

title: Competitive programming
about: Timed contests against everyone else. The fastest way to find your gaps.

links.name: Codeforces
links.about: the main arena. Rated contests several times a month.

links.name: AtCoder
links.about: famously well-written problems and a beginner contest series.

links.name: CodeChef
links.about: long and short contests, strong Indian community.

links.name: HackerEarth
links.about: contests plus hiring challenges.

links.name: Topcoder
links.about: the oldest of them, with algorithm marathons.

links.name: ICPC
links.about: the university team championship. Worth aiming at.

title: Web development and real projects
about: Briefs and sandboxes for building things people can actually open.

links.name: Frontend Mentor
links.about: real designs to build against, with a community review.

links.name: DevChallenges
links.about: full-stack briefs, from a landing page to an app.

links.name: roadmap.sh Projects
links.about: project ideas graded by level, for every stack.

links.name: Full Stack Open
links.about: University of Helsinki's free React and Node course.

links.name: CodePen
links.about: front-end sketchpad; also the best place to read other people's CSS.

links.name: StackBlitz
links.about: full Node projects in the browser, instantly.

links.name: Replit
links.about: collaborative online IDE across many languages.

links.name: JSFiddle
links.about: quick HTML, CSS and JavaScript scratchpad.

title: Git, open source and portfolio
about: The part employers actually look at.

links.name: GitHub
links.about: where your work should live. A tidy profile is a CV.

links.name: GitHub Skills
links.about: short interactive courses run inside real repositories.

links.name: Open Source Guides
links.about: how to contribute without annoying maintainers.

links.name: GitLab
links.about: the alternative, with built-in CI worth learning.

links.name: Bitbucket
links.about: common inside companies using Atlassian tools.

title: Career roadmaps
about: What to learn next, and in what order, for a given job.

links.name: roadmap.sh
links.about: frontend, backend, DevOps, AI, security and more, as visual maps.

links.name: Full Stack Open
links.about: a complete modern web stack, free and graded.

links.name: The Odin Project
links.about: the same ground, project-first.

title: Python, data and AI
about: Notebooks, datasets, models and the papers behind them.

links.name: Kaggle
links.about: datasets, competitions and free GPU notebooks.

links.name: Google Colab
links.about: a free GPU notebook, no setup at all.

links.name: Hugging Face
links.about: models, datasets and demos, all open.

links.name: Papers with Code
links.about: every paper linked to a working implementation.

links.name: DataCamp
links.about: guided data courses. Paid, with a free tier.

title: Databases and SQL
about: SQL rewards practice more than reading. All of these are hands-on.

links.name: SQLBolt
links.about: interactive lessons that take about two hours end to end.

links.name: SQLZoo
links.about: exercises against real datasets, increasing in difficulty.

links.name: Mode SQL Tutorial
links.about: the clearest explanation of window functions anywhere.

links.name: HackerRank SQL
links.about: graded problems, easy to hard.

links.name: LeetCode Database
links.about: SQL questions asked in real interviews.

title: Cloud and DevOps
about: The skills that turn "it runs on my laptop" into "it runs for everyone".

links.name: Microsoft Learn
links.about: genuinely good free training, with certification paths.

links.name: AWS Skill Builder
links.about: Amazon's own courses; many are free.

links.name: Google Cloud Skills Boost
links.about: hands-on labs on real infrastructure.

links.name: Docker
links.about: start with their own getting-started guide, not a video.

links.name: Kubernetes
links.about: the documentation is the best tutorial available.
